title: Celebrating Georg+Otto Friedrich — KARL MAYER’s First Warp Knitting Customer | Textile World
content: + The Association of Italian Textile Machinery Manufacturers (ACIMIT). Some of them have been in existence since the very beginning, and one of them recently celebrated a round anniversary: the first warp knitting machine produced by the innovative textile machine manufacturer based in Obertshausen was sent on 10 September 1948 to Georg+Otto Friedrich, a leading producer of warp-knitted digital printing fabrics and technical textiles in the neighboring town of Groß-Zimmern. Today, Georg+Otto Friedrich is the largest customer of the model of KARL MAYER’s most modern generation of tricot machines, the HKS 3-M ON. Thanks to the high technical level of the machines and the know-how of the employees, the textile products made by Georg+Otto Friedrich are of the highest quality. “As the leading manufacturer of textile solutions in Europe and as the world market leader in the field of digitally printable warp-knitted polyester fabrics, we have a special responsibility for environmental and social issues,” explained Philipp Seubert, managing director of GOF Industrial.

title: Machines
content: He likely developed the warp knitting machine based on the hand warp frame in 1768. The advent of modern technology and the invention of the drive shaft with lifting discs enabled the mechanisation of warp knitting machines starting in 1807. Since their first appearance in Germany in the Mid-19th century, these machines have gone through constant modernisation and further development, in particular in the textile industry region of Saxony, represented by the Hermann Reichenbach machine factory, the August Esche machine factory, the Ernst Saupe knitting machine factory, and others. Visit the Esche Museum in Limbach-Oberfrohna, Saxony, to learn more about the origins of warp knitting and the history of the textile industry! Current textile production uses cutting-edge warp knitting machines to produce modern materials. In particular, production of knit goods from natural textiles such as silk, cotton, linen, or wool is a focus area for machine developers due to the constantly changing consumer market.

title: Warp Knitting Machine | Textile Machines Manufacturer | WUYANG
content: Wuyang Textile Machinery (WUYANG), founded in 1986, is engaged in the R&D, design, manufacturing, sales, and service of textile equipment. We have established a Double Needle Bar Warp Knitting Machine R&D Center, which has designed and developed a series of high-speed, efficient, and intelligent textile equipment. With strong technological and research capabilities, our company has been recognized as one of the top ten technological advancements in China's intelligent manufacturing industry, an enterprise with advantages in intellectual property rights, and a demonstration enterprise for cultivating Chinese industrial brands. In 2012, WUYANG started planning the construction of the first digital shop floor in the Chinese textile machinery industry. Following the requirements of Made in China 2025 and Germany's Industry 4.0, we invested a total of 150 million yuan and built a 35,000 square meter facility. WUYANG’s digital shop floor is designed, constructed, and operated in accordance with the standards of Germany's Industry 4.0 and China's Made in China 2025 initiative.
